Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a concise, clinician-ready historical checkpoint note for my rehabilitation archive summarizing the evidence reviewed on February 19, 2027, that supported advancement beyond the initial 20-minute run-walk restart stage. Include the completed session count, session structure, spacing, and both during-session and following-day symptom checks. Clearly frame this as prior advancement evidence, not as current clearance.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Rehabilitation archive — February 19, 2027 historical checkpoint", "folder": "rehabilitation archive", "body": "Historical checkpoint — evidence reviewed February 19, 2027

Purpose: Prior advancement evidence after the initial 20-minute run-walk restart stage. This note is historical and does not constitute current clearance or alter current rehabilitation limits.

Evidence reviewed:
- Completed sessions: 6 of 6 prescribed 20-minute sessions — January 26, January 30, February 2, February 6, February 10, and February 13, 2027.
- Session structure: 20 minutes alternating 4 minutes of easy running with 1 minute of walking.
- Spacing: Two nonconsecutive sessions per week, with no third weekly session.
- During-session checks: Each session remained free of focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change.
- Following-day checks: No following-day symptoms were reported; ordinary walking and stairs remained symptom-free through the next-day checks.

Checkpoint interpretation: This complete, symptom-free six-session record was the evidence reviewed at the February 19 clinical checkpoint supporting consideration of progression beyond the initial 20-minute restart stage. It should be read as prior advancement evidence only—not as present-day clearance, a new prescription, or authorization for any current activity."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_087_01", "path": "args", "criterion": "The document states that six sessions were completed, that they were nonconsecutive, that each session lasted 20 minutes, and that each used alternating four-minute easy runs with one-minute walks. Missing or contradictory count, duration, spacing, or interval structure must fail.

The document states that every completed session and every corresponding following day remained free of focal pain, swelling, instability, and gait change. It must cover both the during-session and following-day observations; omissions or contradictions must fail.

The document is clearly framed as a concise clinician-facing historical checkpoint describing prior evidence that supported advancement beyond the initial 20-minute restart stage at the February 19, 2027 review. It must not present this checkpoint as current clearance or a current tolerated running level.", "value": {"title": "Rehabilitation archive — February 19, 2027 historical checkpoint", "folder": "rehabilitation archive", "body": "Historical checkpoint — evidence reviewed February 19, 2027

Purpose: Prior advancement evidence after the initial 20-minute run-walk restart stage. This note is historical and does not constitute current clearance or alter current rehabilitation limits.

Evidence reviewed:
- Completed sessions: 6 of 6 prescribed 20-minute sessions — January 26, January 30, February 2, February 6, February 10, and February 13, 2027.
- Session structure: 20 minutes alternating 4 minutes of easy running with 1 minute of walking.
- Spacing: Two nonconsecutive sessions per week, with no third weekly session.
- During-session checks: Each session remained free of focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change.
- Following-day checks: No following-day symptoms were reported; ordinary walking and stairs remained symptom-free through the next-day checks.

Checkpoint interpretation: This complete, symptom-free six-session record was the evidence reviewed at the February 19 clinical checkpoint supporting consideration of progression beyond the initial 20-minute restart stage. It should be read as prior advancement evidence only—not as present-day clearance, a new prescription, or authorization for any current activity."}}]}

It identifies the February 19, 2027 checkpoint as prior evidence supporting progression beyond the initial stage and explicitly says it is not present-day clearance."}]}
